headline: A preprint reports that graph-structured skills improve agent benchmark results over a skill-optimization baseline
summary: A September 18 arXiv preprint represents reusable agent skills as a directed graph of execution steps and context-dependent paths, then optimizes them with population-based mutation and crossover. Across five benchmarks, the authors report higher average success than SkillOpt in three model/harness settings: +4.01 percentage points for GPT-5.4-nano without a harness, +1.76 points for GPT-5.4 without a harness, and +1.33 points for GPT-5.4 with the Codex harness. Results average three optimization runs; GraphSkillEvo is best in 13 of 14 evaluated settings, but trails on GPT-5.4-nano LiveMath. The authors also report lower aggregate optimization-token counts for the two no-harness settings. These are single-preprint results, not independently reproduced.
